title: vllm-project/vllm v0.25.0
event_hint: vLLM v0.25.0 software release featuring prefill/decode disaggregation support via Mooncake connector
problem: LLM serving infrastructure requires disaggregated prefill/decode execution with KV cache transfer between compute stages; vLLM adds Mooncake connector integration for GDN and MLA support.
mechanism: vLLM v0.25.0 integrates Mooncake connector with GDN (Qwen3.5) and MLA (DeepSeek-V4-Flash) support, NIXL Mamba1 support, MultiConnector KV transfer parameters merging, and exposes usage field for disaggregated serving. Secondary-tier implementation for PD disaggregation.

evaluation_context: vLLM inference serving engine release; disaggregated prefill/decode serving via Mooncake connector with GDN and MLA support; distributed inference infrastructure with NIXL and MultiConnector protocols
limitations: Release notes describe disaggregation features but do not provide quantitative network performance metrics (TTFT, TPOT, P95, network utilization, KVCache transfer overhead). No network-side scheduling policies or KVCache location awareness documented. No comparison between network-side optimizations vs pure GPU memory scheduling. Mooncake GDN and MLA performance characteristics not specified.
project_relevance: This source documents vLLM's adoption of prefill/decode disaggregation via Mooncake connector, but lacks the network-aware scheduling and performance metrics that TPN requires. The disaggregation is compute-stage focused (prefill/decode) without evidence of network-side optimization for KVCache transfer, TTFT/TPot reduction, or token performance goals. Not a network-aware solution but compute disaggregation with transport integration.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the TTFT, TPOT, token throughput, or P95 latency improvements from Mooncake-based disaggregation compared to monolithic serving?
